evaluation.positioning_hook: A haunted hunter in fog-choked Edinburgh must rescue a missing child from shape-shifting demons while his own dead brother weaponizes his grief against him.

audience_appeal_marketability.reasoning: The hook is immediate and genre-legible — demons, a rescue mission, and a grief-haunted lead — which gives it a clear horror-action audience. The emotional intensity is strong, but the bleak ending and heavy psychological register narrow the four-quadrant reach.

conceptual_hook_clarity.reasoning: The premise lands early in the quarry mission and the speaking-class demons are easy to grasp as a threat. The title concept and the brother/child choice sharpen the hook, though the mythology takes a few beats to fully settle.

character_appeal_and_long_term_potential.reasoning: Kiaan is built as a damaged, physically formidable lead with a clear wound, and Amyra gives the script a strong counterweight with authority and tenderness. The relationship has real charge, though the supporting cast is more functional than expansive.

creative_originality_and_boldness.reasoning: The Edinburgh setting, the hunter-society infrastructure, and the demons that 'remember for you' give the script a distinct angle inside familiar genre terrain. The final emotional turn into a child-hallucination fight is bold, even if the underlying mythic framework is recognizable.

narrative_momentum_engagement.reasoning: Once the quarry mission starts, the script moves with strong forward pressure and escalating dread, culminating in a major cavern set piece. The middle is more atmospheric than plot-dense, but the rescue objective and emotional countdown keep it moving.

resonant_originality.reasoning: The idea of demons exploiting memory rather than just flesh is a fresh, immediately playable twist, and it pays off in the Tom/Kiaan material. It feels novel enough to stand out, though it still sits within a recognizable monster-hunter framework.

world_density_and_texture.reasoning: The Hunter Society, speaking-class demons, quarry markings, and underground tunnels create a world with rules and hierarchy rather than a generic monster backdrop. The texture is strongest in the operational details and the Edinburgh atmosphere.

tonal_specificity.reasoning: The script has a very specific mournful register: fog, stone, rain, quiet violence, and emotional collapse all live in the same lane. The blend of gothic dread and intimate grief is consistent and hard to mistake for something else.

latent_depth_slow_burn_potential.reasoning: Kiaan’s history with Tom, Amyra’s family trauma, and the demons’ memory logic all suggest a larger emotional and mythic architecture beneath the surface. The script is already explicit about its wounds, but it still implies more history than it fully explains.

relationship_density_and_ensemble_engine.reasoning: Kiaan and Amyra carry the emotional engine well, and Leena gives the world a credible command structure. Beyond that, the ensemble is mostly functional support rather than a relationship web that keeps generating new material.

lead_characters.name: Kiaan
lead_characters.demographics: Male, late 20s, emotionally shut down hunter with a traumatic past and a physically dangerous presence.
lead_characters.hook: Kiaan is a quiet, bruised demon hunter in Edinburgh whose discipline is really a survival strategy for unbearable guilt. He moves like someone who has already lost too much, and the script keeps revealing that his stillness is not calm but containment; the dead brother Tom, the carved tallies, and his reflexive violence all point to a man one trigger away from collapse.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the showcase territory of Joel Edgerton in The Stranger or Michael Shannon in Take Shelter — a contained, internalized performance that can suddenly turn feral. It gives an actor the chance to play silence, shame, physical authority, and a final emotional breakdown that redefines the character.

lead_characters.name: Amyra
lead_characters.demographics: Female, mid-20s, hunter partner with combat skill, emotional intelligence, and a hard-earned protective streak.
lead_characters.hook: Amyra is the script’s emotional blade: sharp, competent, and visibly tired of carrying other people’s damage. She reads as the only person who can get through to Kiaan, which makes her both his anchor and the person most exposed to his fracture; her own family trauma gives her a parallel wound that keeps her from being just a love interest or mission partner.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of role that gave Jodie Comer in Killing Eve or Rebecca Ferguson in Silo a chance to combine physical command with wounded intimacy. It offers a performer a strong action lane, a romantic charge, and a late-story emotional rupture that lands hard.

lead_characters.name: Leena
lead_characters.demographics: Female, mid-40s, Hunter Society authority figure, tactical, unsentimental, and protective of the team.
lead_characters.hook: Leena is the institutional spine of the Hunter Society, the person who can read a room and a liability in the same glance. She’s not written as warm, but she has authority, restraint, and the kind of quiet concern that makes her feel like a veteran who has seen too many people break under pressure.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is strong character-actor material in the vein of Olivia Colman in Broadchurch or Carrie Coon in The Leftovers — a role built on command, subtext, and the ability to make one look carry a whole command center. It gives an actor the pleasure of playing leadership under strain rather than exposition delivery.

lead_characters.name: Gareth MacLeod
lead_characters.demographics: Male, 30s-40s, missing hunter and father under duress.
lead_characters.hook: Gareth is the mission’s human stake: battered, terrified, and carrying the emotional weight of a child taken by the demons. He functions less as a full arc and more as a pressure point that turns the rescue into a moral trap.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of short, high-intensity role that can become a memorable distress performance in the vein of David Dastmalchian in Prisoners or Ben Foster in Hell or High Water. It gives an actor a concentrated burst of fear, guilt, and collapse.

lead_characters.name: Tom
lead_characters.demographics: Male, child, deceased brother appearing as a hallucination/manifestation.
lead_characters.hook: Tom is the emotional ghost at the center of Kiaan’s collapse, first as memory and then as a weaponized presence that keeps returning in different forms. He is not a conventional supporting character so much as the story’s most intimate haunting, and the script uses him to externalize guilt, abandonment, and self-punishment.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of eerie, emotionally loaded child role that can be unforgettable in the way the boy in The Sixth Sense or the child presence in The Babadook is unforgettable. It gives a young performer or voice/physical performer a chance to embody innocence, hurt, and uncanny menace in the same role.

casting_characteristics: One lead with heavy physicality and intense emotional range
One key female partner with action capability and romantic chemistry
Child casting for Tom and the missing child presence

notable_requirements: Converted Hunter Society war room and medical bay
Fog-heavy exterior work and night forest/quarry sequences

technical.vfx_details: Creature transformation work, demon crowd augmentation, hallucination overlays, and a few environment-enhancement moments in the cavern and tunnel sequences.
technical.sfx_needs: Creature makeup/prosthetics, blood effects, practical combat beats, and environmental debris/collapse effects in the quarry and cavern.

platform_fit.series_engine_or_release_model: Feature release model: streamer original or genre theatrical with a mature audience; the violence and emotional darkness fit premium streaming best.

budget.note: The quarry, tunnel, and cavern sequences will drive practical build and lighting costs, and the demon crowd work pushes beyond a simple contained indie. It still reads controllable if the creature count and environment scale are kept disciplined.

casting.note: Kiaan needs an actor who can carry silence, physical combat, and a late emotional implosion, while Amyra has to land both authority and tenderness. The child role for Tom and the hallucination material add a second layer of specificity.

development.note: The memory-driven demon mythology is distinctive, but the script leans heavily on the emotional logic of Kiaan/Tom/Amyra to make the climax land. Buyers will want confidence that the mythology and the character wound are equally legible.

comp_set.title: The Babadook
comp_set.why_it_comps: Like this script, it turns grief into a literalized horror engine and makes the monster feel psychologically personal.

comp_set.title: Underworld
comp_set.why_it_comps: The secret-war creature mythology, leather-and-stone visual language, and action-horror lane are close to this script’s commercial neighborhood.

comp_set.title: A Dark Song
comp_set.why_it_comps: The occult dread, emotional austerity, and contained, ritualized descent into darkness match the script’s tone and scale.

comp_set.title: The Ritual
comp_set.why_it_comps: The foggy, isolated terrain, creature threat, and male grief under pressure are strong tonal and audience comps.

comp_set.title: The Night House
comp_set.why_it_comps: The script shares its haunted-psychology approach, where the supernatural threat is inseparable from the protagonist’s internal fracture.

audience_target.primary_audience: Adult horror fans who want emotional stakes with their creature action, especially viewers drawn to grief-driven genre films and gothic atmospherics.
audience_target.demographics: Skews 18-44, slightly male but not exclusively, with strong appeal to genre-literate streaming audiences and prestige-horror viewers.

budget_tier.note: Contemporary setting and a manageable cast keep it in indie territory, but the quarry/cavern builds, creature work, and night exterior volume push it above micro.

lane_fit.detail: This sits naturally in the lane of elevated creature horror with a strong emotional spine and a clear visual identity. The script offers enough action and mythology for genre buyers while still feeling actor-forward and prestige-adjacent.

ip_potential.detail: Standalone feature: the Kiaan/Tom wound is the engine, but the script does not present a clean sequel or spinoff vector beyond this story.

strengths.what_it_means: That twist gives the script a sharper commercial identity than a standard demon-hunt and makes the horror feel emotionally invasive rather than just physical. Buyers chasing elevated genre will see a clean hook for marketing and performance-driven casting.
strengths.evidence: The demons 'remember for you,' the quarry markings reference buried fear, and Tom keeps returning as a weaponized hallucination.

strengths.dimension_or_area: Kiaan is a real lead role
strengths.what_it_means: The role has the kind of internal contradiction that can attract a serious actor and elevate the whole package. That matters because a buyer can sell this as a showcase for a performer who can do silence, violence, and breakdown in one turn.
strengths.evidence: His quiet opening kill, the carved tallies, the Tom hallucinations, and the final collapse into feral violence all define the part.

strengths.dimension_or_area: Amyra gives the story a human counterweight
strengths.what_it_means: Her competence and emotional clarity keep the script from becoming a solo mood piece and give the movie a second face for audience attachment. That broadens the casting conversation and makes the relationship marketable as more than just genre utility.
strengths.evidence: She leads the mission, grounds Kiaan in the tunnels, kisses him, then becomes the emotional casualty of his choice.

strengths.what_it_means: The fog, stone, tunnels, and old-city geography create a strong visual brand that can be sold in stills and trailer language. It also keeps the production from feeling anonymous, which helps both buyers and audiences remember it.
strengths.evidence: Old Town Edinburgh, St. Gideon’s grounds, Blackcross Quarry, and the subterranean cavern all carry a unified gothic texture.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The climax escalates to a true event beat
strengths.what_it_means: The cavern battle and final Tom confrontation give the script a trailer-friendly third act with a big emotional and physical payoff. That combination is what lets a genre buyer justify the spend and gives the movie a memorable ending image.
strengths.evidence: Amyra’s blinding, Kiaan’s rampage, and the final playground fight all land as distinct set pieces.

whats_special.headline: This is a grief-driven creature-horror feature with a strong actor showcase at its center and a visually saleable Edinburgh gothic world around it. The memory-based demon mythology gives it a fresher commercial angle than a standard monster hunt, while the contained contemporary footprint keeps it in a buyer-friendly indie lane.

items.area: The mythology arrives through atmosphere more than rules.
items.detail: The speaking-class demons, memory theft, quarry markings, and 'choosing' language are compelling, but the script leaves a buyer doing some interpretive work to understand the system. That is manageable for genre audiences, but it makes the premise feel more experiential than fully pitch-clean on first pass.

items.area: Kiaan’s turn at the quarry is a hard audience test.
items.detail: The child-versus-man choice, followed by the throat-grab on Amyra, is the script’s sharpest emotional rupture and the moment that most defines whether viewers stay with him. It is powerful, but it also makes the lead morally volatile in a way that narrows sympathy before the finale.

items.area: The supporting ensemble is functional, not generative.
items.detail: Leena, Gareth, Murphy, and the other hunters establish the world, but they do not yet create a relationship web that keeps producing new story energy. For a buyer, that means the movie lives or dies primarily on Kiaan/Amyra/Tom rather than on a broader ensemble engine.

items.area: The cavern finale is creature-heavy by indie standards.
items.detail: The demon crowd, practical combat, hallucination overlays, and environment work all stack into a sequence that will need disciplined execution to stay inside the tier. It is still controllable, but the climax is where the production can most easily drift upward if the creature count expands.

issues.headline: The script’s biggest friction is that its strongest emotional turn is also its riskiest: Kiaan’s quarry choice and breakdown are memorable, but they make the lead harder to embrace in the moment. The other buyer-level concern is execution discipline — the mythology is cool, but the finale’s creature and cavern demands will need tight scope control to preserve the indie lane.
